samples.question: A set of short dark line segments is drawn as a ring on a white canvas, placed end to end with small gaps between neighbours. Wherever two neighbouring segments nearly meet they count as connected; if every consecutive pair nearly meets all the way around, the whole ring closes into ONE single loop. An 'open' drawing, by contrast, has one place where the chain is broken by a much larger, clearly visible gap, so the segments do NOT form a loop. Does the drawing form a single closed loop? Choose: closed or open.
